articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: DNA left on a protective painting cover helped investigators recover two stolen Renoirs and uncover what they suspected were preparations for another art heist, a French prosecutor said Monday.
articles.title: DNA and vehicle-tracking help French investigators recover stolen Renoirs

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Actor and disability rights advocate RJ Mitte, who brought a lifetime of experience with cerebral palsy to fictional family struggles in an essential role on "Breaking Bad," died Monday at age 34.
articles.title: RJ Mitte, 'Breaking Bad' actor and disability rights champion, dies at 34

articles.author: Brian Mann
articles.description: Katie Zacharia worked for one of Trump's companies and raised her profile appearing on conservative-leaning talk shows. She also amplified right-wing conspiracy theories. Now she'll be the president's chief spokesperson.
articles.title: New White House press secretary a 'devoted fan' of Trump and MAGA

articles.author: Tamara Keith
articles.description: Nearly $22 million in taxpayers funds has been spent to air the ads, with nearly half spent after Trump promised to fund what the White House calls public service announcements through his super PAC.
articles.title: Government spent $10 million on pro-Trump ads after president said super PAC would fund

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Authorities say Blair was physically abusive and injured two flight attendants while traveling from Los Angeles to New York. A Blair representative said she had a medical emergency aboard the plane.
articles.title: Actor Selma Blair removed from plane by police after altercation

articles.author: Luke Garrett
articles.description: The Justice Department says the search is part of an "ongoing federal investigation", while Omar calls it "an attempt to target political enemies"
articles.title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's DC home, DOJ says it approved the warrant

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Opposition parties say revisions to the list of eligible voters favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party. Authorities have removed more than 130 million names from the voter roll.
articles.title: India's opposition parties march to top court as protests over voter lists escalate

articles.author: Ann Powers
articles.description: "I just want to make people really feel things about the world they live in," Grian Chatten says of Dopamine Chamber, which he describes as the band's attempt to map the tensions of our moment.
articles.title: Fontaines D.C.'s decadent, dystopian vision of our time

articles.author: Tonya Mosley
articles.description: Ali plays a devout Muslim family man, who also happens to be an assassin in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. After decades in the business and two Oscars, he says he has less fear as an actor.
articles.title: Mahershala Ali is still hungry as an actor: 'Let's fail on camera until we find it'

articles.author: Jaclyn Diaz
articles.description: The U.S. government is trying to end the dominance of high-quality, low-cost drones made in China. But more restrictions mean higher costs for cash-strapped police forces that rely on those drones.
articles.title: U.S. restrictions on Chinese drones are hurting cash-strapped police departments

articles.author: Ben Doherty (now) and Krishani Dhanji (earlier)
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Robert Pether has stressed his innocence and recalled his brush with death in his first comments since the Australian engineer departed Iraq after serving more than five years in jail.
Pether and his Egyptian colleague Khalid Radwan were detained in Baghdad in 2021 after flying in for a meeting with bank officials to resolve a dispute with his engineering firm, CME Consulting.
We were innocent when we were taken on the 7th of April 2021, and we remain innocent today.
I was released from prison hours away from death. My body was shutting down after months of critical illness and excruciating pain, but I remained trapped in Iraq.
She is an incredible person, someone that I have so much respect for, and being able to come home was incredible. Just the emotion that it brings is, you can’t describe it. I mean, it’s been years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian politics live: Climate protester restrained after interrupting NSW parliament; Albanese says he’ll do whatever he can to stop ‘abhorrent’ US execution live stream

articles.author: Mollie Reilly and Sian Cain
articles.description:
Actor who played Walter White Jr on the acclaimed show and advocated for disability representation remembered by Bryan Cranston as ‘my sweet son’

RJ Mitte – a life in pictures

The Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte died on Monday aged 34, his representatives confirmed.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” Mitte’s representatives said in a statement. “Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RJ Mitte, actor best known for Breaking Bad, dies aged 34

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Exclusive: Homes demolished along east coast after being deemed too vulnerable to live in, figures reveal
Seaside communities along the east coast of England have lost at least 183 homes to coastal erosion and landslides over the past 16 years, figures obtained by the Guardian reveal.
After councils judged properties across the Yorkshire and East Anglian coasts too vulnerable to remain safely occupied, the homes were proactively demolished.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Coastal erosion in England has claimed at least 183 homes in past 16 years

articles.author: Rob Cameron in Bratislava
articles.description:
Case of couple who wed legally in Austria exposes clash between EU court ruling and national restrictions
A same-sex couple are suing authorities in Slovakia for refusing to register their Austrian marriage, testing whether a landmark EU court ruling can turn recognition abroad into legal security at home.
Their fight exposes a clash between European obligations and national restrictions – and what that means for LGBTQ+ people living under Robert Fico’s populist-nationalist government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Same-sex couple sue over Slovakia’s refusal to register marriage

articles.author: Hettie O'Brien
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: The prime minister is calling for closer ties with the EU, but what could this actually amount to?
Good morning. After a holiday spent contracting nursery bugs from an 11-month-old, it’s good to return. Yesterday, Andy Burnham marked his first day back after party conference by calling for a closer relationship with the EU and drawing a line under a decade of “drift and division”. On Sunday, he said it was “clear” the Kremlin had been involved with the 2016 Brexit referendum vote.
Both statements mark a break, rhetorically at least, from his predecessors. Conservative governments long insisted there was no evidence of Russian interference in the Brexit vote. Keir Starmer attempted to put the entire issue of Brexit behind him, treating it as a historic event rather than a cause of economic pain.
UK | Andy Burnham said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps were “almost certainly” behind threats to RAF Fairford, the firmest attribution of responsibility made so far by the UK after an incident late last month.
UK politics | A close adviser to Nigel Farage had an influential role at a national polling company despite not being publicly associated with the firm, the Guardian revealed.
Ukraine | Volodymyr Zelenskyy has vowed to respond to Russia’s continuing attacks on the Ukrainian power grid as European leaders rally around Kyiv amid a feud with Donald Trump over Ukraine’s strikes on oil refineries.
Israel | Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the documentary NAZA and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.
US news | RJ Mitte, the young actor best known for playing Walter White Jr in the award-winning TV series Breaking Bad, died on Monday. He was 34.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tuesday briefing: Could Burnham take Britain back towards the EU?

articles.author: Patrick Commins and Jonathan Barrett
articles.description:
‘Round-up’ pricing in items such as coffee suggests increases are exceeding the typical 1.5% surcharge fee

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Businesses are using the recent ban on credit card surcharges as “cover” to pass along much larger price increases to customers, experts say, as cafes and restaurants struggle to cope with climbing costs and rising interest rates.
Credit card surcharges, typically worth about 1.5% of the transaction, were banned from 1 October, as part of a Reserve Bank-led reform aimed at improving transparency for customers and, ultimately, lowering bank fees.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Card surcharge ban used as ‘cover’ for larger price increases by Australian businesses, experts say

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Security forces use helicopters to rescue dozens of people as the two storms damage infrastructure and cause flash flooding
At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel pummelled Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes.
Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man who died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo in the southern state of Guerrero, governor Evelyn Salgado said at a press conference.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five people on Mexico’s Pacific coast

articles.author: Guardian staff and agency
articles.description:
Six Flags says nine rollercoasters across six amusement parks temporarily closed after reported fatal incident on Goliath ride in Georgia
Theme park company Six Flags temporarily closed nine rollercoasters across six amusement parks on Monday after one person died and several others were injured in an incident involving a coaster in Georgia.
A spokesperson for the park said they closed similar attractions across their parks “out of an abundance of caution” after the incident at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24km) north-west of Atlanta.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Death on Six Flags rollercoaster in US triggers ride closures across six states

articles.author: Catie McLeod
articles.description:
Aircraft taken out of operation after flight from Perth after the discovery of parasitic insects on board 
Qantas has been forced to ground a plane in Rome after bedbugs were discovered on the aircraft on its way from Perth.
The parasitic insects were found in the front of the economy section of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner as it made its way from Perth to Rome for the QF5 flight on 9 October, a source with knowledge of the incident confirmed on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bedbug infestation forces Qantas to ground plane in Rome

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Over 10m people have tuned in for episodes of new season of BBC hit as mass TV audiences become increasingly rare
For the celebrities chosen as traitors in the BBC’s juggernaut reality show, the task is simple – kill off fellow contestants without getting caught.
Yet with the new series of Celebrity Traitors once again attracting huge audiences, its UK producers are delighting in one of the show’s more wholesome qualities – its popularity is staving off the death of television’s ability to unite the nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Universal appeal’: Celebrity Traitors producer reveals secrets to its success

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Cambridge University study suggests stark gender divide in misdiagnosis, with women also waiting longer for treatment
Women with autoimmune conditions are up to 74% more likely than men to be told their symptoms are psychological or psychosomatic, and face much longer waits for a diagnosis and treatment, a study suggests.
Hundreds of millions of people – about one in 10 globally – are affected by autoimmune conditions, which can cause a range of health issues including fatigue, muscle pain and rashes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Women ‘more likely to be told autoimmune conditions are psychological’

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
ZyMix platform has contract with Tencent, which US alleges has links to People’s Liberation Army
A new messaging and payment “super app” marketed at British students uses servers owned by a Chinese company that has been put on a US military blacklist for its alleged affiliation to the People’s Liberation Army.
ZyMix, which is being pushed on university campuses as the UK’s first super app designed “for gen Z”, combining chat, payments and community features, has a contract with a German-based subsidiary of Tencent Holdings, a Chinese conglomerate in Shenzhen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Super app’ aimed at UK students uses servers owned by Chinese firm on US blacklist

articles.author: Maya Yang in New York and Sian Cain
articles.description:
Actor, who allegedly punched one Delta attendant, bit another and tried to open plane door, was charged for two separate assaults after the plane landed
The actor Selma Blair was arrested on Sunday at John F Kennedy airport in New York after she allegedly attacked two flight attendants on a Delta Air Lines flight, and separately charged with two counts of assault for allegedly kicking a police officer and a nurse after landing.
Blair’s arrest happened at about 11pm, after Port Authority of New York and New Jersey officials said they responded to a call “about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Air Lines flight 938 which was parked at the gate” at JFK after arriving from Los Angeles.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Selma Blair charged with assault of police officer and nurse after allegedly attacking flight attendants

articles.author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok
articles.description:
High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks

IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

The threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is putting world financial stability at risk, the International Monetary fund has warned.
In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted the sky-high valuations for AI companies along with their increasing debt pile as one reason that risks in the system are “elevated”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
National park officials took the precautionary measure to limit tourist access after heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate
Heavy rainfall fuelled by a supersized El Niño weather pattern briefly forced Argentinian authorities to close tourist access to the famed Iguazu Falls, amid fears that rapidly rising water levels would cause the river to burst its banks.
National park officials took the precautionary measure on Monday when the Iguazu River’s flow exceeded 12,000 cubic metres per second – more than six times its average rate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Argentina temporarily closes Iguazu Falls after El Niño-fuelled surge in water levels

articles.author: Penry Buckley
articles.description:
Media adviser who married federal One Nation MP in 2023 confirms she has started working part-time for the party’s state executive

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Vikki Campion, the News Corp columnist and wife of the federal One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce, has begun working as an adviser for the party in New South Wales in the lead-up to the March state election.
Campion, who helped the NSW One Nation leader and candidate for Cessnock, Mike Newman, with a press conference in the Hunter electorate on Tuesday, told Guardian Australia she had started working for the party’s state executive as a contractor, providing media advice on a part-time basis this week.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Vikki Campion, News Corp columnist and wife of Barnaby Joyce, begins role with NSW One Nation

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Defence also cross-examines witness over postmortem examinations of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A bullet hole left in a bedroom door and DNA found in the barrel of the firearm have been scrutinised in court as Beau Lamarre-Condon’s double murder trial continues in Sydney.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bullet hole in door and DNA evidence scrutinised in Beau Lamarre-Condon double murder trial

articles.author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok
articles.description:
World Economic Outlook says states’ oil stocks are low and budgets are overstretched, as it upgrades UK GDP growth forecast for 2026

Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF

The global economy “could soon test the limits of resilience”, as emergency oil stocks run low and government budgets become overstretched, the International Monetary Fund has warned.
In its twice-yearly World Economic Outlook, the IMF said global growth had withstood the Middle East conflict better than feared over the past six months.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

articles.author: AFP
articles.description:
Leftist former leader accused of involvement in shooting of three Europeans in Santa Cruz and torture of two others
Bolivia’s attorney general has announced an investigation into leftist former president Evo Morales, alleging his involvement in the murder and torture of European citizens in 2009.
Seventeen years ago, police raided a hotel in the city of Santa Cruz, shooting dead Eduardo Rózsa Flores, a Bolivian-Croatian, Michael Dwyer, an Irishman, and Árpád Magyarosi, a Hungarian-Romanian.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bolivia investigates ex-president Evo Morales over alleged ties to 2009 killings

articles.author: Guardian staff and agency
articles.description:
Timothy Broglio says Catholics on army firing squad should ask to be excused since it clashes with church teachings
The archbishop who oversees the spiritual care of Catholics serving in the US military condemned the Pentagon’s proposed plans to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan later this year.
Archbishop Timothy Broglio also stipulated in a Monday statement that any Catholic soldier assigned to the US army firing squad should ask to be excused from that duty, which he described as contrary to the teachings of the church. He joins other Catholic leaders in speaking out against the death penalty and the live stream plans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Archbishop of US military condemns Pentagon plans to livestream execution

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Jennifer Rankin and Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
PM hails next month’s ‘reset’ summit as first step to closer ties, but tensions over trade may prove problematic
Andy Burnham has promised a “serious dialogue” over the UK’s future place in Europe, saying the existing relationship is “not good enough” as he framed next month’s Brussels summit as a possible first step to EU membership.
The prime minister said Britain must take a “clear-eyed rational look” at its long-term relationship with the bloc to boost economic growth and control immigration, which needed to go beyond Labour’s existing red lines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham promises ‘serious dialogue’ over UK’s relationship with EU

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Top House Democrats question the ‘corrupt weaponization’ of federal government against Trump’s adversaries
Ilhan Omar’s Democratic colleagues have condemned federal agents’ search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home on Monday morning, describing it as “deeply disturbing” and emblematic of the Trump administration’s “corrupt weaponization” of the US government.
House Democratic leaders, including minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, party whip Katherine Clark and caucus chair Pete Aguilar, issued a joint statement excoriating the president for the search.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats rebuke federal raid of Ilhan Omar’s home: ‘rogue abuse of power’

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
articles.description:
Luca Olmetto was trapped roughly 10 metres below ground in the Gorroppeddu cave in the Urzulei mountain range
A 31-year-old man has been pulled alive from a cave on the Italian island of Sardinia after being trapped roughly 10 metres below ground for 26 hours following a rockslide.
In a huge and complex operation, rescuers worked non-stop after Luca Olmetto became trapped in the Gorroppeddu cave in the rugged Urzulei mountain range in central-eastern Sardinia on Sunday afternoon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man rescued from cave on Sardinia after being trapped by rockslide for 26 hours

articles.author: Jasper Jolly in Paris
articles.description:
Bosses of Citroën owner and French carmaker also urge UK government to consider limiting imports from China
Stellantis and Renault have backed the UK car industry for inclusion in proposed rules to protect EU industry, but urged the British government to consider limiting imports of Chinese cars.
Emanuele Cappellano, who leads Stellantis’s European brands including Fiat, Citroën, Opel and Vauxhall, and François Provost, the chief executive of France’s Renault, said the UK should effectively be counted as one of the EU’s 27 member states for the purposes of the proposed “Made in Europe” legislation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stellantis and Renault back UK to get EU car industry protection

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breaches stretched defences

Why are the Houthis attacking Saudi airports and how are the missiles getting through?

Saudi Arabia has been forced to suspend all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh until next Saturday after a further round of Houthi missile attacks caused more damage and left one person dead. Some airlines, including Gulf Air and Bahrain Air, had already said they were cancelling flights until next Saturday. More missiles were fired at Saudi Arabian cities by the Houthis on Monday, Saudi Arabian’s military spokesperson said.
The Gulf nation announced it was suspending flights from Riyadh, its second busiest airport, after Houthi missiles killed 13 people on Saturday and left more than 300 injured. Saudi state TV broadcast CCTV footage that showed passengers deluged in smoke and falling masonry as they queued at the airport terminal to board a plane just as the Houthi missile struck.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia further suspends flights after latest deadly Houthi attack on airport

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Thousands join rally to deliver petition calling for resignation of election commissioner
Delhi police have again obstructed protests in India’s capital as thousands of people returned to the streets, led by opposition leaders, to demand the resignation of the election commissioner.
After mass unrest in the capital over the weekend, when thousands were detained and harassed by police as they attempted to take part in a protest led by the gen Z Cockroach movement, on Monday the main opposition leaders led another procession through Delhi, this time to the supreme court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian opposition figures lead march to police barricades around supreme court

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
A businessman wanted in the US for allegedly bribing top Venezuelan officials has been taken into custody
A businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody.
Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro. The US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the state department had been offering a reward of up to $10m for information leading to his arrest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fugitive businessman taken into US custody in Venezuela bribery case

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Israeli PM calls for criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in Guardian-produced documentary
The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the investigative documentary NAZA and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.
The award-winning documentary, directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza. The film is in cinemas, including in the UK and the US, and will be shown in more than 50 countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NAZA: Netanyahu orders identification and prosecution of film’s interviewees

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Brussels uses WTO rules to quickly impose quota, which will halve Chinese market share to 3%

Business live – latest updates

VW boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic industry

The EU is to limit the number of hybrid electric vehicles imported from China to 350,000 cars a year, the European Commission has confirmed.
Imports have been soaring in the past two years; about 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids are likely to be sold this year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year

articles.author: Ed Walton and James Parrish for MetDesk
articles.description:
Clear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean Sea

Europe live – latest updates

Temperatures fluctuated dramatically in the Balkans last week, with unusually large differences between daytime highs and overnight lows – known as the diurnal range.
An area of high pressure over the region brought prolonged sunshine during the day, while clear skies at night allowed temperatures to drop rapidly as heat escaped into the atmosphere without cloud cover to slow the cooling.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Balkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for Greece

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
President Zardari suspends provincial government in escalation of tensions as Khan supporters march to Islamabad
Politicians from ⁠the party of the former Pakistani ​prime minister Imran Khan have been detained after the suspension of a provincial government now under emergency rule.
Pakistan’s president declared a state of emergency and suspended the ⁠government in north-western Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, led by Khan’s ally Sohail Afridi, on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan detains hundreds of politicians from Imran Khan’s PTI party

articles.author: William Christou in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Unidentified projectile strikes King Khalid airport, killing one and injuring 11, as escalating attacks threaten to draw more countries into Yemen conflict

Analysis: attack will force rethink of Trump strategy

A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday, the day after a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people.
An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport, starting a fire, killing one person and injuring 11, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. It was the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say

articles.author: Marina Dunbar (now) and Frances Mao (earlier)
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed. You can read our latest full report here:

Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say

Some more Gulf reaction to Houthi’s deadly airport attack and continued threats to target Saudi airspace.

 In a significant message, the United Arab Emirates has issued a statement in solidarity with Saudi Arabia – expressing support for “all measures aimed at safeguarding the kingdom’s security and stability”.
The UAE message is improtant given the major rupture in relations this year between the two oil-rich kingdoms, first sparked by lingering divisions in Yemen, and made worse by the Iran War and arguments over oil prices which led to the UAE quitting OPEC (currently led by the Saudis) after six decades of membership.
Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East crisis: Riyadh airport hit again as Houthis claim attacks, including strike that killed 12 – as it happened

articles.author: Jasper Jolly in Paris
articles.description:
Oliver Blume says ‘Made in Europe’ rules to counter rapid rise of lower-price Chinese brands ‘must reward real value creation’
The boss of Volkswagen has backed EU proposals to boost its domestic industry, arguing European carmakers need to be able to “compete under comparable conditions” with Chinese rivals.
Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Volkswagen boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic European industry

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Authorities impose strict lockdown in capital to try to stop rally against removal of 130m names from electoral roll
Indian authorities have placed Delhi under a severe lockdown and detained tens of thousands of people, including the leader of the youth-led “Cockroach” movement, in an attempt to stop an anti-government protest.
Thousands of people from across India were blocked from attending the demonstration, which had been called by the “Cockroach Janata party” (CJP) to protest against an exercise that has stripped 130m names from India’s electoral roll.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cockroach’ leader among thousands detained in Delhi protest crackdown

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchers
A controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week.
It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime vaccine opponent.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Controversial vaccine trial touted by RFK Jr gets go-ahead in Guinea-Bissau

articles.author: Julian Borger and Rachel Savage
articles.description:
Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza

The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza.
The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law

articles.author: Adam Morton in Nadi, Fiji
articles.description:
‘The climate issue is the security issue,’ says Turkish minister at Pacific pre-Cop summit in Fiji
Wealthy countries should spend far more on dealing with the climate crisis than the 5% of GDP promised by Nato members for defence because “the climate issue is the security issue”, the host of the next UN summit has said.
But, in comments that are likely to prove contentious, the Cop31 president-designate, Murat Kurum, hedged on whether countries should try to repeat a previous agreement to “transition away from fossil fuels” – the primary cause of the climate crisis – when they meet in Turkey next month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cop31 host urges wealthy countries to spend ‘much more’ on climate than defence

articles.author: Megan Davies for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding
Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
As a result of the strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season

articles.author: Nino Bucci Courts and justice reporter
articles.description:
Employee had also been in Bali when he told his manager he was working from home, Fair Work Commission hears

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney currency trader who was sacked for working from Singapore without approval has won an unfair dismissal case, but failed to be awarded compensation.
The Fair Work Commission ruled on Wednesday that Charles Graham had been unfairly dismissed by HIFX Australia, trading as Xe, in December last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sydney trader sacked for working from Singapore without permission wins unfair dismissal case

articles.author: Saher Ahmed in Cairo
articles.description:
Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood
Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention.
Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Thousands expected to march in Delhi on Saturday, as anger mounts over controversial changes to voter lists in world’s largest democracy 
India’s Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which began as a satirical movement but is now emerging as a political force among gen Z’s, says authorities have begun detaining its members en masse days before a major anti-government protest in Delhi.
Opposition parties, their student units, and the “Cockroach” youth movement have been holding almost daily demonstrations seeking the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a controversial revision of ⁠voter lists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ party accuses government of mass detention of members ahead of weekend protest

articles.author: South West News Service
articles.description:
Free-roaming Aldabra population far exceeds human population of Seychelles after decades-long recovery programme
A survey of the world’s largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has discovered that the once endangered species is thriving.
A population of Aldabra giant tortoises lives on an island in Seychelles called Aldabra Atoll.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scientists discover 180,000 giant tortoises on one Seychelles island

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Responding to a Guardian report that revealed thousands of tonnes of fuel was transported to Russia, Seoul said it was investigating the cases
South Korea will take legal action if it finds that shipments of fuel from its ports to Russia broke domestic law, the government has said, responding to a Guardian report on the trade.
The government, in a statement issued by the foreign and trade ministries and the customs service, said that it is “checking additional information concerning the loading cases reported by the Guardian” and “if the verification establishes that our laws and regulations have been violated, it plans to act in accordance with the law”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea threatens legal action if fuel shipments to Russia found to have broken law

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
The country’s 85-medal haul included athletes who trained with limited money and borrowed equipment. Plus, the Mumbai performer turning everyday absurdities into comedy
In a country where cricket eclipses every other sport, the recently concluded Asian Games offered a much-needed reminder of India’s breadth of sporting talent. In this edition of the games, in Japan, India won 85 medals: 21 golds, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. I admit I did not know many of the players competing, or even some of the sports they play before putting this piece together. Learning about the stories, I wonder why not.
There were individual breakthroughs, records broken and history made. There were also hard-fought team victories, including the Indian women’s hockey team gold medal after a 44-year wait.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From competing for food to a gold medal: the stories behind India’s Asian Games winners

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Top House Democrats question the ‘corrupt weaponization’ of federal government against Trump’s adversaries
Ilhan Omar’s Democratic colleagues have condemned federal agents’ search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home on Monday morning, describing it as “deeply disturbing” and emblematic of the Trump administration’s “corrupt weaponization” of the US government.
House Democratic leaders, including minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, party whip Katherine Clark and caucus chair Pete Aguilar, issued a joint statement excoriating the president for the search.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats rebuke federal raid of Ilhan Omar’s home: ‘rogue abuse of power’

articles.description:
The prime minister tells MPs the next summit with the EU will be held on 20 November
Burnham to urge MPs to embrace closer ties with EU
Zia Yusuf, Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson, is speaking now. He started his speech with an account of a 73-year-old woman dying in North Wales after having to wait 23 hours for an ambulance, and he sought to link this to immigration.

The Royal College of Emergency Medicine estimates that 15,000 people across Britain died last year due to excess wait times for emergency treatment. That’s 300 people a week, 300 lives destroyed, 300 families devastated.

I don’t think that’s because he wants to have a fight over the European Union. I think that’s because he knows what we’re talking about today impacts hard in what is known as the red wall.

articles.title: Burnham says ‘public will be the boss’ in any future decision about closer relationship with the EU – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Ana Reyes demands Trump officials explain East Potomac tree cutting and says it will likely cause ‘irreparable harm’
US district judge Ana Reyes on Monday ordered a 24-hour halt to tree cutting at the historic East Potomac golf course while she decides on an emergency order from plaintiffs concerned that Donald Trump’s plans for the course are moving forward despite a pending court case challenging them.
“Tree removal for routine maintenance is not exempt from this order,” Reyes’ wrote. “Plaintiffs are likely to suffer immediate and irreparable harm in the absence of preliminary relief.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Judge halts tree removal at Washington golf course Trump eyes for expansion

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Pete Hegseth | Pre-loved | Marlborough man | Canterbury tale | Newt kids on the block
Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, has authorised the livestreaming of an execution by firing squad (Report, 9 October). Morally this is no different from a terrorist group posting a video of a beheading. It marks yet another step in the brutalising of American society under the second Trump administration. Britain stopped holding public executions in 1868.
John Boaler
Calne, Wiltshire
• I find nearly all the “pre-” expressions irritating, but the term pre-loved (Letters, 7 October) is, in this one instance, justifiable. Items that have been passed on due to the owner’s lack of affection are exactly in a state of “pre‑lovedness”, waiting for the buyer who will truly cherish them.
Paola McClure
Dundee
 Continue reading...
articles.title: If the US livestreams an execution, it will be an act of terror | Brief letters

articles.author: Matt Shuham
articles.description:
Trump and key allies have accused Omar of immigration fraud, and have called to expel her from the country
Federal agents searched Representative Ilhan Omar’s home on Monday morning as part of a criminal investigation, according to the Department of Justice and reports in the Associated Press and Fox News.
In a social media post later on Monday, Omar criticized the raid as an attempt by the Trump administration “to target political enemies and weaponize law enforcement” and said she would “not be silenced”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ilhan Omar says she will not be silenced after federal agents raid her home

articles.author: Walker Bragman and Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Children’s Health Defense and RFK Jr publicly dispute recent measles deaths to ‘distract’ from damage caused and question vaccines, experts say
The six-year-old girl at the children’s hospital in Lubbock, Texas, burned with fever and struggled to breathe. Doctors soon put her on a ventilator, snaking a thick tube down the child’s throat so a machine could breathe for her; they placed IVs to rehydrate her tiny body and they prescribed antibiotics for any bacterial infections that may have taken hold in the weeks she had spent at home battling measles.
But it was too late. Within a day of being ventilated, the child went into shock, her blood pressure crashed and she went into cardiac arrest. She could not be resuscitated. Her family, and the nation, mourned: she was the first child to die of measles in the US in a decade.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anti-vaxxers target Texas measles doctors to cast doubt on deaths amid outbreak

articles.author: George Chidi
articles.description:
Gwinnett county is home to many immigrants and other newcomers, and how it votes could be decisive for Congress
Johanna Park might just be an ambassador for Gwinnett county, Georgia, one of the 10 most ethnically diverse counties in the United States.
Park owns Cafe Amico at Suwanee Town Center, one of her three Italian coffee shops in the area just north of Atlanta. She was born in Korea and lived much of her life in Argentina and Peru. She’s been in Gwinnett for more than 20 years, part of an early wave of Korean immigration that’s built Korean American car dealerships, banks, insurance agencies, supermarkets and restaurants like her own. It’s also a population that’s increasing in influence and not just numbers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: This Georgia county is one of the US’s most diverse – and that could flip multiple elections

articles.author: Maanvi Singh
articles.description:
From restaurants to farms to healthcare, the US president’s hardline policies have reshaped Americans’ daily lives
If there is one campaign promise that Donald Trump has kept, it is his pledge to deliver “mass deportations”.
Two years later, voters are living uneasily with the consequences.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How immigration is molding the US midterms: ‘Trump has gone too far’

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
In a recent visit to Greece, the secretary of state suggested that Europe must rediscover the values of conquest and expansion
They had obviously worked hard on the backdrop – and it was magnificent. On 7 October, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, delivered a major speech in Athens, outdoors, with the Acropolis behind him. The sun was setting, bathing the ancient scene, including the Parthenon, in the light of the golden hour.
The golden hour, but yet not quite the golden age. This was not Pericles defending democracy. Instead, Rubio offered a haunting vision of the choices facing the west, arguing that the US and Europe must rediscover the values of exploration and conquest that once drove centuries of expansion, or face decline and irrelevance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marco Rubio is promoting troubling ideas about ‘Western civilization’ | Ted Widmer

articles.author: Nesrine Malik
articles.description:
The latest attack by Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia may prove to be more calamitous for the region than the world imagines
On Saturday, Houthi rebels launched a shocking and deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s capital city, Riyadh. At the time of writing, the missile strike on King Khalid international airport has killed at least 13 people and left 300 injured, marking a significant turn in a regional conflagration that is only getting more intense. It was the single most deadly attack on any Gulf country since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. In Saudi Arabia, a country that is unaccustomed to such fatalities, the death toll is bewilderingly high and likely to prompt a bloody response.
Over the past year, the Gulf has entered a new era of instability that is not temporary and cannot be reversed. This may feel like an overstatement – casualties have been relatively low, after all, compared with Gaza and Iran – but the gradual erosion of peace and security in places such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE has changed the region more dramatically than its leaders would like to acknowledge.
Nesrine Malik is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Gulf has entered a new era of instability. If its leaders think they can rely on old alliances, they are wrong | Nesrine Malik

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
A fuel deal with Vladimir Putin, and sanctions against the legal institution, ram home the president’s belief that might is right
On Friday, Donald Trump drove home his belief that might is right and the rule of law is an obstacle rather than an essential foundation stone of international order. First came the escalated assault on the international criminal court (ICC), sanctioning the body itself. Then he announced a deal with Russia to buy diesel.
The US has long chafed at the notion of being bound by the rule of law that it espoused publicly. That hypocrisy now appears as a lesser vice. The president has declared that “my own morality” is all that constrains him. His brazen flouting of the law, embrace of dictators and rhetorical attacks all undermine global standards.
Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on the US, Russia and the international criminal court: Trump’s assault on the rule of law intensifies | Editorial

articles.author: Eric Berger
articles.description:
As raw milk industry experiences record growth, experts say it might contain pathogens that can sicken people
As raw milk becomes increasingly popular among Americans, there have been several recent disease outbreaks tied to the product, alarming public health officials.
Last week, the American Academy of Pediatrics called for a ban on sales of unpasteurized milk in the United States.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Physicians’ group calls for ban on raw milk – as it’s becoming increasingly popular in the US

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Austin Sarat ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
The execution of a former US army psychiatrist by firing squad is to be livestreamed after Pete Hegseth said it would be a public event. Nidal Hasan was sentenced to death after killing 13 people at a military base in Texas in 2009. There has been widespread condemnation of the decision, including from the UN which said it would ‘amount to torture’. Lucy Hough speaks to US academic and capital punishment specialist Austin Sarat, the author of Life After Death: Surviving Execution 
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Barbaric’ firing squad livestream ordered by Pete Hegseth - The Latest

articles.author: Judith Levine
articles.description:
Political parties vie for Jewish support based on false assumptions about a single issue: Israel
Everybody wants the Jewish vote. As if there were one. Jews are educated, generally liberal. Although they comprise only about 2% of the electorate, they vote in high numbers, overwhelmingly for Democrats. In 2024, 79% chose Kamala Harris. They are also assumed to be steadfast friends of Israel, no matter what it does. Republicans, waging a fake war on antisemitism while courting white supremacists, consider Jews increasingly up for grabs.
Nationally, Jewish Americans are concentrated in a few bright blue spots. A 2020 map from the Jewish Electorate Institute showed a third of Jews living in 20 congressional districts – out of 435 – most of them in New York, New Jersey, California and (purple) Florida. Of these, only one sent a Republican to Washington.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stop talking about the US ‘Jewish vote’. It's not that simple | Judith Levine

articles.description:
Donald Trump’s latest campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas, was rocked by repeated protests as the US president urged Texas voters to back the embattled Senate candidate Ken Paxton. At least half a dozen demonstrators interrupted the US president during his speech, with some led away by police. One was physically assaulted by a Trump supporter as he tried to leave the arena. The Republican campaign to maintain control of the Senate has become increasingly focused on Texas, where the Democrat James Talarico has emerged as a serious threat
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters removed after disrupting Trump rally in Texas – video

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Charles Blow and Shrai Popat , produced by Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
The biggest question in US politics may be whether Democrats can ever win in the south. In this year’s midterms, Georgia has once again emerged as a bellwether. The state has shifted from deep red to purple for the last several election cycles and remains a frontline state in the battle over voting rights. In a recent Stateside with Kai and Carter live event in collaboration with On Air Presents, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman were joined by Guardian contributing writer Charles Blow and political reporter Shrai Popat for a lively conversation about everything at stake in Georgia – including why Jon Ossoff needs Keisha Lance Bottoms to win the governor’s race if he hopes to run for president in 2028, what Donald Trump might do to intervene in the election, and how any voter suppression moves could backfire in the south.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Could Trump’s plan to suppress voters backfire in the south? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Laure Boulinier, Sofia Couceiro and Boglarka Kosztolanyi
articles.description:
The US midterms may not be as much of a spectacle as the presidential elections, but they are just as important and can completely change not just the course of a presidential term, but federal legislation for years to come. The Guardian unpacks how these elections work, what the results mean and how they affect American life

articles.title: US midterms: what are they and why do presidents dread them? – explainer

articles.author: Anna Tims
articles.description:
It is billing £32.99 a month but I have had no functioning phone line since it switched me to Digital Voice
I’ve had no landline since May 2025 when BT switched it to Digital Voice. Weeks passed, and each call to BT involved at least an hour waiting on hold and answering security questions before being passed between departments.
Eventually, last December, two engineers were sent and discovered that a wire had been severed during the upgrade. They said they needed a cherry picker to reconnect it to its original location and would return. They did not.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BT charged me for more than a year despite landline being dead

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Exclusive: Homes demolished along east coast after being deemed too vulnerable to live in, figures reveal
Seaside communities along the east coast of England have lost at least 183 homes to coastal erosion and landslides over the past 16 years, figures obtained by the Guardian reveal.
After councils judged properties across the Yorkshire and East Anglian coasts too vulnerable to remain safely occupied, the homes were proactively demolished.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Coastal erosion in England has claimed at least 183 homes in past 16 years

articles.author: John Collingridge
articles.description:
Some of Britain’s wealthiest financiers, including Sir Paul Marshall, have given a platform to critical coverage or are linked to its leading opponent
“This is virtue signalling,” said Nigel Biggar. “These are elites who are trying to demonstrate that they are being progressive.”
The target of his scorn was one that has obsessed him for years: the movement to pay reparations for the slave trade, and specifically the Church of England’s plan to spend £100m atoning for its involvement.

articles.title: Lobbying, lawyers and a media blitz: the fight to kill the Church of England’s £100m slavery compensation fund

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor

Cambridge University study suggests stark gender divide in misdiagnosis, with women also waiting longer for treatment
Women with autoimmune conditions are up to 74% more likely than men to be told their symptoms are psychological or psychosomatic, and face much longer waits for a diagnosis and treatment, a study suggests.
Hundreds of millions of people – about one in 10 globally – are affected by autoimmune conditions, which can cause a range of health issues including fatigue, muscle pain and rashes.

articles.title: Women ‘more likely to be told autoimmune conditions are psychological’

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
ZyMix platform has contract with Tencent, which US alleges has links to People’s Liberation Army
A new messaging and payment “super app” marketed at British students uses servers owned by a Chinese company that has been put on a US military blacklist for its alleged affiliation to the People’s Liberation Army.
ZyMix, which is being pushed on university campuses as the UK’s first super app designed “for gen Z”, combining chat, payments and community features, has a contract with a German-based subsidiary of Tencent Holdings, a Chinese conglomerate in Shenzhen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Super app’ aimed at UK students uses servers owned by Chinese firm on US blacklist

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Over 10m people have tuned in for episodes of new season of BBC hit as mass TV audiences become increasingly rare
For the celebrities chosen as traitors in the BBC’s juggernaut reality show, the task is simple – kill off fellow contestants without getting caught.
Yet with the new series of Celebrity Traitors once again attracting huge audiences, its UK producers are delighting in one of the show’s more wholesome qualities – its popularity is staving off the death of television’s ability to unite the nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Universal appeal’: Celebrity Traitors producer reveals secrets to its success

articles.author: Heather Stewart in Bangkok
articles.description:
High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks

IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

The threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is putting world financial stability at risk, the International Monetary fund has warned.
In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted the sky-high valuations for AI companies along with their increasing debt pile as one reason that risks in the system are “elevated”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Richard Adams
articles.description:
Surge in EHCP applications poses risk to public finances and may lead to deteriorating levels of support
Councils are warning of potentially “catastrophic” debts, which are forecast to reach a record £10bn over the next 18 months, as a result of rapid growth in demand for special educational needs and disability (Send) support in English schools.
Although the government recently cleared more than £5bn in historic council Send debts, a surge in requests has led to authorities predicting they will have re-accrued that debt figure by April, and doubled it by 2028.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: English councils warn of ‘catastrophic’ Send debts forecast to hit £10bn by 2028

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Plans for a new theatre for world’s longest-running soap in Digbeth scrapped as part of cost-cutting measures
The BBC is set to stop recording The Archers in Birmingham for the first time in the show’s 75-year history, after scrapping plans for a radio drama theatre that was to be the new home of the world’s longest-running soap opera.
A pledge to move recordings to the so-called Tea Factory, the BBC’s new Birmingham hub in Digbeth, has become the latest victim of the corporation’s £500m cuts plan.

articles.title: BBC to stop recording The Archers in Birmingham for first time in its 75-year history

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Jennifer Rankin and Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
PM hails next month’s ‘reset’ summit as first step to closer ties, but tensions over trade may prove problematic
Andy Burnham has promised a “serious dialogue” over the UK’s future place in Europe, saying the existing relationship is “not good enough” as he framed next month’s Brussels summit as a possible first step to EU membership.
The prime minister said Britain must take a “clear-eyed rational look” at its long-term relationship with the bloc to boost economic growth and control immigration, which needed to go beyond Labour’s existing red lines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham promises ‘serious dialogue’ over UK’s relationship with EU

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Home secretary also expands police support ‘with immediate effect’ for high-profile public figures not currently MPs
Security arrangements for high-profile public figures including politicians and members of the royal family are to be urgently reviewed after the killing of Ann Widdecombe, the home secretary has said.
Shabana Mahmood said former MPs, party leaders who are not MPs, peers, former members of devolved parliaments and party spokespeople will also be offered police support.

Bosses of Citroën owner and French carmaker also urge UK government to consider limiting imports from China
Stellantis and Renault have backed the UK car industry for inclusion in proposed rules to protect EU industry, but urged the British government to consider limiting imports of Chinese cars.
Emanuele Cappellano, who leads Stellantis’s European brands including Fiat, Citroën, Opel and Vauxhall, and François Provost, the chief executive of France’s Renault, said the UK should effectively be counted as one of the EU’s 27 member states for the purposes of the proposed “Made in Europe” legislation.

articles.title: Stellantis and Renault back UK to get EU car industry protection

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Prime minister has reopened the debate over whether Russia sought to influence the 2016 referendum
Andy Burnham unexpectedly reopened an old Brexit debate when he said he had been told after becoming prime minister that Russia had interfered in the 2016 EU referendum.
It was a contentious issue in the second half of the previous decade, but one that had largely been forgotten about as the UK finally adjusted to the reality of leaving the EU. Now Burnham’s comments have given the topic a fresh impetus.

articles.title: How significant are Burnham’s remarks on Kremlin interference in Brexit vote?

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Farage’s party says it would ‘embed’ immigration enforcement in UK and use ‘aerial imaging’ to identify people

UK politics live – latest updates

Children and mothers would not be exempt from plans by Reform UK to immediately deport 90,000 asylum seekers and impose a five-year ban on people being granted asylum.
The party’s most hardline immigration policies to date were condemned by refugee charities and others as “unworkable” and an abandonment of Britain’s tradition of helping victims of war after they were announced by Nigel Farage on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Children and women included in Reform plan to immediately deport 90,000 asylum seekers

articles.author: Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
US economists developed models that help central bankers and finance ministers to stabilise their economies

Business live – latest updates

Two US economists have won the 2026 Nobel economics prize for their work developing models that help central bankers and finance ministers to stabilise their countries, avoiding long recessions and runaway inflation.
Robert Hall of Stanford University, California, and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, New York, were recognised for developing the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation”, giving policymakers better tools to smooth out the peaks and troughs of their economies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nobel Prize for economics awarded to Hall and Woodford for work on ‘smoothing’ crises

articles.author: Henry Dyer and Rowena Mason
articles.description:
Exclusive: Chris Bruni-Lowe used Redfield & Wilton Strategies role to develop potential campaign tactics, sources say
A close adviser to Nigel Farage had an influential role at a national polling company despite not being publicly associated with the firm, the Guardian can reveal.
Chris Bruni-Lowe, Farage’s private pollster for many years, played an important role in the operations of Redfield & Wilton Strategies and used it to develop potential campaign strategies, according to several sources who have worked there.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revealed: Nigel Farage adviser had unpublicised role at polling firm

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Survivors had criticised ‘outrageous’ appointment of Laura Johnson to £150,000 job with Barnet Group
A housing director who oversaw cost cutting at Grenfell Tower before the fatal fire has left a £150,000-a-year senior council housing role after a backlash from bereaved families and survivors.
Laura Johnson was the director of housing at the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) at the time of the 2017 Grenfell fire which killed 72 people, and was criticised in the subsequent inquiry for her role in budget-cutting decisions prior to the blaze.

articles.title: Ex-director who oversaw Grenfell cost-cutting leaves council housing role after backlash

articles.description:
Exclusive: Finds suggest account in medieval folklore of a camp near Frenni Fawr hill was rooted in reality
Magnus Maximus, the Roman emperor who ruled Britain in the fourth century, led his troops against the Picts and Scots, but a theory that he also established a military camp near Frenni Fawr hill in Wales has so far been based on folklore.

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Roman fort found in Wales could prove myth of emperor’s camp is real

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
Calls for planned fuel duty rise to be scrapped as analysis finds average fuel bill could hit £1,965, up from £1,294
Millions of British van drivers face a combined £2.5bn cost to cover the rising price of diesel this year, according to figures, fuelling calls for the government to scrap its planned fuel duty rise.
The owners of diesel vans and pickups can expect to collectively spend almost £8.5bn at the pump this year, according to analysis for the Guardian, after diesel prices climbed to record highs due to a global fuel shortage caused by disruption to refineries in the Middle East and Russia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK van drivers face extra £2.5bn in diesel costs this year, figures show

articles.author: Rob Davies and Simon Lock
articles.description:
Accountancy firm Deloitte Cyprus among those that appear to have backdated records outlining the Russian billionaire’s assets
Aides of Roman Abramovich – including staff at the global accountancy firm Deloitte – falsified paperwork mapping the oligarch’s sprawling offshore business empire, records suggest, helping his businesses dodge tax and disguise assets.
New analysis of leaked corporate records uncovers what appears to have been a long-running and carefully orchestrated strategy of backdating documents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Roman Abramovich aides falsified paperwork to disguise assets and dodge tax, records suggest

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
The production marks the Hollywood director’s first play written for the stage,  which he will also direct
Sacha Baron Cohen will headline Quentin Tarantino’s play The Popinjay Cavalier when it premieres on the West End in London in March 2027.
The production marks the Hollywood director’s first work written for the stage – which he will also direct.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen to star in Quentin Tarantino’s West End play The Popinjay Cavalier

UK Health Security Agency notes above-average activity and urges at-risk groups to get vaccinated
Flu is striking earlier than usual in England, experts have said, insisting that vaccination is the best way to blunt its impact.
According to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), flu is at low levels, but various metrics, such as the proportion of positive tests and GP consultations for influenza-like illness, suggest it is on the rise, with the number of emergency-department attendances for influenza-like illness above seasonally expected levels.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flu cases higher than usual in England during September, experts say

articles.author: Matthew Weaver
articles.description:
Actor says he should have made a joke of his admission, he felt institutionalised there and he is not watching the series
Richard E Grant has said his early exit from The Celebrity Traitors was due to his failure to realise his fellow contestants would take him seriously.
The Withnail and I actor was voted off as a traitor after brazenly admitting his status to other contestants.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Richard E Grant admits Traitors mistakes: ‘I never thought they would take me seriously’

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
As ‘one in, one out’ scheme ends, refugees still want to cross the Channel despite French police aggression and hostile welcomes
The smuggler works quickly. Using a small shovel, he digs up a dinghy buried in a sand dune on a beach not far from Boulogne-sur-Mer, assembles it and affixes a motor in record time.
“I never saw anyone work like this,” says Amad, from Iraq, one of a group of about 30 asylum seekers waiting to cross the Channel. “The UK government wants to stop the smugglers, but they are smart. They have plan A, plan B and plan C, so there is always a way for them to get people across this sea. For as long as asylum seekers will pay them, there is too much money involved for them to give up.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is there a different way to fix the small boats crisis?

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Although there is scepticism about Tehran’s capabilities, it has become clear it wants Britain to feel it poses a risk
Britain may have been only peripherally involved in the bombing of Iran that Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu started, but in the past fortnight it has become clear that Tehran wants to pose a threat inside the UK in response.
In the aftermath of the confused incident near RAF Fairford, western officials are weighing up whether to warn publicly that Iran now has US military targets in Europe on its mind, such as the air force base in Gloucestershire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: After RAF Fairford incident, how big a threat to the UK is Iran?

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty with Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor; produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke Smith; executive producers Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
Are we really living through ‘end-times fascism’? Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor think so.
In a new series from the Guardian, the pair speak to Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty in an extended interview. From Trump 2.0 and the rise of the tech billionaires to Gaza and the climate emergency, Klein and Taylor argue we are not just lurching from crisis to crisis but are in a new and dangerous moment in history. But they haven’t given up hope of a fightback
You can watch the full interview with Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor here.
Aditya’s suggested reading:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s End Times Fascism is out now and available here. It began life as a special essay in the Guardian, which you can read here.
A different take on whether Trump 2.0 is fascist comes from the economist Branko Milanović on his brilliant Substack.
Elon Musk gives Donald Trump millions, and Trump gives Musk vast access to power. To read more, look at Quinn Slobodian and Ben Tarnoff’s long read for the Guardian and their recent book Muskism: A Guide for the Perplexed.
For some phenomenal reporting on Trump’s second term, look at Regime Change by Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan.
How did the business class learn to love Trump and embrace chaos? Paul Heideman gives a lucid analysis in his recent book Rogue Elephant.
Klein and Taylor’s book regularly cites Karen Hao’s Empire of AI.
There’s also The Nerd Reich, just out from Gil Durán.
If you enjoyed Yanis Varoufakis in our last episode of Radical Thinking, check out his book Technofeudalism.
As for how AI is imposing a new age of total corporate control, The Rulers by Cecilia Rikap is a must.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gaza is a moral tear in the universe’: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty – podcast

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
Tories plan to scrap low-carbon housebuilding, Greens back new nuclear reactors, and Labour put oil-drilling decisions on hold
New homes could be built without solar panels, heat pumps and high-grade insulation, leading to higher household bills if the Conservative party wins the next general election.
Kemi Badenoch made scrapping the future homes standard (FHS) one of the central planks of her bid to become the next prime minister at the Tory party conference this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We need less point scoring’: What party conference season taught us about UK climate action

articles.description:
Zack Polanski has lost the Holborn and St Pancras byelection to Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali. Despite the Greens increasing their vote share from 2024, Polanski had the cloud of the ‘Zionism is racism’ row hanging over his head.
Now there are questions over his leadership and whether he can steer the party through the ongoing Zionism row. Will the Greens remain a fringe party?
You can watch this episode on the Politics Weekly YouTube channel here.
